name: Two Largest Supports Force a Permutation Structure in Protected Covers
statement: Consider $m$ distinct punctured-cube pieces satisfying the protected-cover equations, and suppose two supports have the largest possible size $m-1$. Their supports are $K\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{a\}$ and $K\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{b\}$ with $|K|=m-2$. The protection labels from the two pieces define a permutation $\pi$ of $K$. If $C$ is its moved set and $c=|C|$, then $c\ge2$; every other support indexed by a moved label has size at least $c$, every fixed-label support has size at least $c+2$, and every such support has size at least three.
proof: The protector equations in both directions force the two supports to differ only in their private labels and make both lists of labels enumerate their common core $K$. Symmetric-difference identities show that a third support contains both private labels and all moved coordinates except its two corresponding labels. This gives the rank bounds and identifies the disagreement set with the moved set of $\pi$, which cannot have size one. The only possible rank-two equality case forces a third missing tip into one of the original punctured cubes, contradicting the cover condition.
